minutes.headline: Select Board voted to commit $150,000 of ARPA funds for the tax assessment investigation and abatement staffing.
minutes.summary: A short special meeting. The board ratified a new public safety desk clerk and signed the police union contract. It then voted to allocate funds to bring in outside help for the FY23 property valuation investigation and a surge of abatement applications. The chair read the public statement on the investigation.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at start; none offered.
Public comment invited again near close; none offered.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Kennedy Jackson as full-time public safety desk clerk
Allocate $150,000 (as heard) from board funds to augment town staff for abatement applications, amended to include tax assessment investigations

budget_items.topic: Funding for tax assessment investigation and abatement support
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair asked the board to commit funds for outside assessors, administrative support and extra abatement processing, with itemized spending to be reported later. The ceiling was based on the town manager's inquiries to vendors.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and fifty thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: The funds were confirmed as coming from ARPA.
A high-volume year is about 50 abatements; 500 are projected. About 50 had been received by Thursday, with many more expected after a Saturday workshop.

decisions.decision: Investigation framework and supporting documents are to be held confidential until the investigation is complete, with board members able to review them in the office.
Board will give public updates twice a month on the investigation; next update February 7, 2023.
RFP for independent assessors can be published now that funding is secured; itemized cost lists will be given to the board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to allocate a sum from ARPA funds, as heard, for outside help on the tax assessment investigation and for abatement applications.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a full-time public safety desk clerk.
Investigation framework and supporting documents will stay confidential until the investigation ends; board members may review them in the office.
The board will give public updates twice a month on the investigation, with the next on February 7, 2023.
An RFP for independent assessors can now be published because funding is secured.

why_it_matters: The money comes from federal ARPA funds on the board's own authority, so the investigation and the surge of abatement applications are paid for without a new tax levy or a town meeting vote.
Residents with an FY23 assessment who file an abatement application will be handled by added outside staff, since about ten times the usual volume of applications is projected.
The investigation's working documents stay closed until it finishes, so the twice-monthly public updates are the main way to follow it.
watch_next: Public update on the investigation on February 7, 2023.
Publication of the RFP for independent assessors, and the itemized cost lists the board is to receive.
